sections.content: You know *primero*, *luego*, *después* and *por último* from A1, and *a continuación* from B1 Unit 24. In a talk or an essay you often want something a little more formal that also tells the listener how many points are coming. *En primer lugar* ("firstly"), *en segundo lugar* ("secondly") and *en tercer lugar* ("thirdly") number each point, a bit like the numbers in a list. The series ends with *por último* ("lastly"), which you know already, or *en último lugar*.

sections.title: A series of three points
rows: En primer lugar, quiero hablar del precio.
Firstly, I want to talk about the price.
En segundo lugar, hablaré del barrio.
Secondly, I will talk about the neighbourhood.
En tercer lugar, hablaré del transporte.
Thirdly, I will talk about transport.
Por último, les pediré su opinión.
Lastly, I will ask for your opinions.

sections.content: You also know *por un lado* from B1 Unit 23. Use *por un lado … por otro* when you have two points, not a longer list: the first half announces that a second half is coming.

items.spanish: Por un lado, el piso es barato; por otro, está lejos del centro.
items.english: On the one hand, the flat is cheap; on the other, it is far from the centre.

items.spanish: En primer lugar, el barrio es tranquilo; en segundo lugar, hay un parque cerca.
items.english: Firstly, the neighbourhood is quiet; secondly, there is a park nearby.

sections.content: These markers open their sentence and are followed by a comma. Stay in one family inside a series (*en primer lugar … en segundo lugar … por último*) and use *por último* only after at least two earlier points. Note *primer*, not *primero*: the short form goes before the masculine noun *lugar*.
